Anthropic prices initial public offering

Anthropic prices initial public offering

AI 作者 surprisetalk 热度 417 回复 788 2026/11/19 07:30
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • Today Anthropic, PBC priced its initial public offering of its Class A common stock at $83.00 per share. The offering consists of 980,000,000 shares of Class A common stock, 956,351,354 of which are being sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 of which are being sold by certain selling stockholders. Anthropic will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders.The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026 under the symbol “ANT.” The offering is expected to close on November 20, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. In addition, Anthropic has granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 147,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock.A registration statement relating to these securities was declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 18, 2026. The offering is being made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the final prospectus may be obtained, when available, from: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, NY 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10014, or by email at prospectus@morganstanley.com.Today’s announcement does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation, or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction.

greycol 2026/11/20 03:47
The 'AI company' Allbirds is 11 years old... Putting out ages of business as if it reflects the maturity of the market or business is a little silly. AI harnesses as a general term basically emerged this year (open claw was first published in nov 2025). ChatGPT only released nov 2022 claiming ages longer than that reflects any form of stability seems beyond generous.

The better point is those companies listed never had a positive revenue before (or after) their IPO while Anthropic has had at least a few profitable quarters (though you'd really like a fiscal year to rule out the more obvious shenanigans). Though the bigger questions remain around the broader market and what that means for income and depreciation (amusingly because of the supply crunch the 'wildly optimistic' deprecation assumptions around GPUs that AI companies have been making have held true (technically you could argue they're appreciating assets, though that won't be the case if data centers start getting liquidated).)
